nodes.label: Fault 10: A command in the manual but not on the instrument

attributes.rationale: SCPI instruments log unrecognised commands to an error queue and carry on, leaving the previous setting in force while the code believes it configured the instrument. Prevention is to probe once at connect and cache what the instrument accepted rather than trusting the manual. A guessed query is worse than a guessed command because it is never answered, times out and latches the transport, so an unconfirmed query is not sent at all.
attributes.evidence: :ABOR exists on the 2400 family and is rejected by the GSM with -113 Undefined header

nodes.norm_label: fault 10: a command in the manual but not on the instrument

attributes.rationale: On the 2400 family MEAS? expands to :CONFigure + :READ?, silently resetting ranging and compliance to *RST values on every point, so the operator's compliance is replaced by the reset default while the file records the requested one. Prevention is to use :READ? against the configuration already in place. The B2901A is the deliberate exception because its manual documents :MEAS? as measuring under conditions already set, and because :READ/:INIT are what trigger its automatic output-on.
attributes.evidence: Deviation 11; found by reading the original 2401 and 20H10 scripts

nodes.label: Fault 4: Source levels rounded before sending

attributes.rationale: round(V, 4) quantises to 100 uV, which is invisible at +-1 V and collapses 21 requested points to 3 distinct levels at +-100 uV. Prevention is to send the full-precision level and let the instrument round - every driver was checked and rounds up, because rounding down would clamp the level - and to record what came back rather than what went out.

nodes.norm_label: fault 4: source levels rounded before sending

attributes.rationale: With [:SENSe]:FUNCtion:CONCurrent off only one function is measured and the other reply field is filled from the source setting, so a 4-wire rig silently returns a 2-wire measurement with the right columns and the wrong physics. Prevention is to enable concurrent measurement in the configuration block on every run and read back both columns; the tell is a measured voltage that matches the commanded one to six figures.

NPLC only cancels mains hum if the instrument knows the mains period, so an integration time set without :SYSTem:LFRequency is worth less than it looks and degrades every reading in a way that resembles sample noise. Set it in the driver's reset block; on the 2611A read first and write only on disagreement, because writing linefreq explicitly disables automatic detection permanently in nonvolatile memory.

nodes.label: Fault 15: A limit sent before the range that has to hold it

attributes.rationale: On the U2722A a compliance value is clamped to the range active when it arrives and *RST leaves the smallest range selected, so a sweep runs with a compliance a hundred times lower than the one on screen while the file records the requested value. Prevention is to widen the range first, now a formal requirement of the ranging contract rather than a habit. Necessary and not sufficient: on the GSM-20H10 setting a range is itself what destroys the compliance. The 2635B is exempt because source.limitY always autoranges for the limit setting.
attributes.status: Closed on the U2722A; the general coupling remains open (fault 23)

nodes.norm_label: fault 15: a limit sent before the range that has to hold it

nodes.label: Fault 21: Asking about the wrong quantity

attributes.rationale: The B2901A's compliance_tripped() read :SENS:CURR:PROT:TRIP? unconditionally, but compliance is always on the quantity you are not sourcing, so that question is right only when sourcing voltage. Sourcing current - which van der Pauw and Hall both do - the current protection is genuinely untripped and the instrument answers 0 honestly to the wrong question, producing a confident False from a safety-adjacent query. Prevention is to read :SOUR:FUNC:MODE? and ask about the matching protection rather than tracking the mode locally, since a remembered copy is one reset or one front-panel press from being wrong.
attributes.evidence: Deviation 21; nothing could have caught it from the outside - the fake returned a tripped flag regardless of mode and the checkup only asked with the output off

nodes.norm_label: fault 21: asking about the wrong quantity

nodes.label: Fault 5: Sweep completion slept rather than polled

attributes.rationale: sleep(round(points * delay * 1.3)) reads the buffer after a guessed interval; round() puts the wait on a whole-second grid so a 10-point 0.1 s sweep waited 1 s, and the original's waitcomplete() was written without a read so it never blocked at all. A partly-filled buffer reads as a complete short sweep. Prevention is to poll the instrument's own reading count, using a wall-clock deadline as a liveness bound rather than as a schedule.

nodes.norm_label: fault 5: sweep completion slept rather than polled

attributes.rationale: np.arange(start, stop, step) assumes the instrument hit every requested level exactly, so every instrument-side reason the real levels differ - rounding, range clipping, a compliance clamp - becomes invisible in the one place anybody would look. Described as the fault with the widest reach. Prevention is to read back what was actually sourced and store that; the software sweep reads back every level it sources for this reason. An exactly arithmetic x column is the tell that it was computed rather than measured.

nodes.label: Fault 13: State left behind by a sweep

attributes.rationale: The GSM's staircase sets TRIG:COUN to the sweep length and puts the source in MODE SWE, and neither was restored - so the next level-set is read as a sweep endpoint and the software fallback meant to rescue a failed sweep returned five plausible points all at 0 V. The recovery path inherits the damage, landing the failure where the code is least exercised. Rule: anything a sweep changes, a sweep must put back, on every exit path including the failing one.

nodes.norm_label: fault 13: state left behind by a sweep

nodes.label: Fault 14: Output state assumed across a source-function change

attributes.rationale: The 2400 family drops the output when the source function changes; with auto output-off disabled (so a sweep holds its level) the instrument is then asked to measure with the output off and :READ? blocks forever with no error. A hang has no diagnostic and reads on the bench as a broken cable. Prevention is to call output_on() after set_source_function(), documented on BaseSMU.set_source_function for every driver, and to read the output state back rather than tracking it locally.
attributes.status: Closed in the experiments and in tools/smu_checkup.py

nodes.norm_label: fault 14: output state assumed across a source-function change

nodes.label: Fault 11: A command the instrument accepts and then ignores

attributes.rationale: The GSM accepts FORM:ELEM VOLT,CURR, queues no error, keeps sending three columns, and answers FORM:ELEM? with the list it was given rather than the one it sends - so neither the command nor the read-back describes reality. Worse than fault 10 because the error queue stays clean and no artefact says the setting did not take. Prevention is to derive the reply layout from the reply itself: count what arrived and take the ratio against the buffer's reading count as the stride.
attributes.evidence: Deviation 50, found by running finished drivers against real instruments

nodes.norm_label: fault 11: a command the instrument accepts and then ignores

nodes.label: Fault 12: A setting that only applies before something is armed

attributes.rationale: TRAC:FEED cannot be changed while buffer storage is active and FORM:ELEM behaves the same way, so sent afterwards they are accepted and do nothing. Order matters even when nothing complains, which makes the fault invisible in a diff that only moved a line. Prevention is to configure before arming and before energising (house rule 12), with the ordering held by state-transition traces.

nodes.norm_label: fault 12: a setting that only applies before something is armed

nodes.label: Fault 6: Instrument state inherited rather than set

attributes.rationale: Sensing, NPLC, compliance and output-off mode persist between runs, so a setting made inside only some code paths leaves the run inheriting whatever the last path left - the IV original set SENSE_REMOTE only in the periodic path, making a single sweep 4-wire after a periodic run and 2-wire after a reset. Prevention is to set everything that matters on every run, in the configuration block, before the output goes on (house rule 12).

nodes.norm_label: fault 6: instrument state inherited rather than set

nodes.label: Fault 16: One range list standing in for two

attributes.rationale: A driver declaring current_ranges makes everything assume source ranges and measure ranges are the same set, but the 2635B measures to 100 pA and sources only to 1 nA - so a measure-only range offered as a sourced level is silently clamped while the arithmetic downstream stays exact. Prevention is to separate source and measure axes throughout the ranging contract, with RangePlan carrying four axes rather than two. The conflation went unnoticed across every earlier driver because the 2635B was the first instrument here where the two differ.

nodes.norm_label: fault 16: one range list standing in for two

nodes.label: A note records what was measured, not what was inferred

attributes.rationale: An unprobed mechanism is worse than a non-discriminating probe because it leaves no failed assertion behind to notice. The GSM-20H10's 2026-08-20 session believed three plausible unprobed mechanisms (rear-panel interlock, source auto-clear, ambiguous channel suffix on :OUTPut) and one reached the instrument note as fact and had to be retracted; the U2722A sub-count round repeated it by reading values before they had settled. Hence: unprobed material goes under Open questions with the question written out, and a retracted hypothesis is deleted rather than archived, because left in place it reads back later as a finding.

nodes.norm_label: a note records what was measured, not what was inferred

attributes.rationale: Asks about compliance while the instrument is riding its limit, the moment where the answer is not already known; paired with fakes that compute compliance from state rather than returning a hardcoded value.
Asks how many readings the buffer holds, counts the numbers that came back, and takes the ratio as the stride - arithmetic cannot lie where a readback can.
Carries four axes rather than two so source ranges and measure ranges are declared separately, because an instrument can measure below what it can source.

Connecting to whatever VISA lists first makes the instrument choice a coin toss in a room with several SMUs, and the file records the experiment rather than which box answered - which is why it explains otherwise-inexplicable historical results. Prevention is the connection panel: the operator picks the address and the run records it, and no code path opens "the first one". Retained after closure because it is worth knowing when old data looks wrong.
Documents for every driver that output_on() must be called after set_source_function(), because the 2400 family drops the output on a function change.

Exposes GPIB0::1::INSTR through GPIB0::30::INSTR as manual candidates distinct from discovered resources, so no address is represented as detected and none is selected implicitly; address 0 is omitted because the direct controller occupies it.
Replaces sentinel values in place rather than filtering them out, because omission would shift later columns left and mis-assign current into the voltage position.
Sends an inferred spelling and then reads SYST:ERR? to establish whether the instrument actually accepted it, caching the answer at connect.

nodes.label: Fault 19: A probe asked where the answer is already known

attributes.rationale: The commissioning checkup called compliance_tripped() at tier 2 with the output off, where False is the honest answer and a method that always returns False passes exactly as well as a correct one. Called the most-repeated fault in the project's history and the only one that can hide all the others, because a test that passes whether or not the code works leaves every fault beneath it undetected. Detection is mutation: break the code on purpose and watch the check go red; then ask whether the fake can even produce a value on the wrong side of the assertion. Prevention is to ask at the moment the answer is known and known to be the interesting one.
attributes.status: Recurring by nature; the specific checkup instance is closed

nodes.norm_label: fault 19: a probe asked where the answer is already known

nodes.label: Fault 22: Direct GPIB-HS address picker was empty

attributes.rationale: The direct transport intentionally returns no instrument resources from list_available() because it can discover the USB controller but does not scan the IEEE-488 bus, and the connection panel used that discovery result as the combobox contents - turning the correct "do not invent discovered instruments" rule into an empty picker. The failure is in the layer that reports rather than the layer that works, so every diagnostic points at the wrong place. Fix is to separate what discovery found from what the operator may type: address_choices() offers GPIB0::1 through GPIB0::30 as manual candidates while _refresh() leaves the discovery result unchanged, address 0 omitted because the direct controller uses primary address 0, and connect() remains the validation authority.

nodes.norm_label: fault 22: direct gpib-hs address picker was empty

nodes.label: Fault 18: An accuracy that is an implementation detail, not a guarantee

attributes.rationale: The maths modules averaged with built-in sum(), which is Neumaier compensated summation on CPython 3.12+ and not on 3.11, moving a fitted intercept enough to fail an exact-comparison golden on one bench machine. The accuracy was real but accidental - a property of one interpreter version, not of the language. The bench machine ran 3.11 because pyproject.toml declared requires-python >=3.10, a floor nobody had ever run. Generalises to: a constraint nothing tests is not a constraint. Prevention is math.fsum (documented to return the correctly rounded sum) over sum(), keeping the built-in only for integer counts where fsum would wrongly return a float.
attributes.status: Closed; floor is 3.14 and every machine runs it

nodes.norm_label: fault 18: an accuracy that is an implementation detail, not a guarantee

nodes.label: Fault 3: NAN and overflow sentinels treated as data

attributes.rationale: "No reading" returns as a number (+9.91e37 NAN, +9.9e37 over-range) that nothing distinguishes from a measurement, so one sentinel dominates a least-squares sum and the goodness-of-fit statistic is computed against the same corrupted set. Replacement must happen in place rather than by filtering, because dropping a value by omission shifts every later column left and promotes the current into the voltage's position.
attributes.status: Closed fleet-wide, enforced by a registry-driven test

nodes.norm_label: fault 3: nan and overflow sentinels treated as data

nodes.label: Fault 17: A default that is never sent is a default nobody chose

attributes.rationale: format.asciiprecision resets to 6 significant figures on every 2600B - below what the Hall measurement needs - and no driver had ever set it, so truncated precision propagates into every derived quantity looking like measurement noise. A reset default that happens to be acceptable is indistinguishable from a chosen value until a firmware revision moves it, so load-bearing defaults are sent explicitly even when they already hold the wanted value; several writes in the 2635B reset are deliberate no-ops against current firmware. This is state inherited from the factory, distinct from state inherited from a previous run.

nodes.norm_label: fault 17: a default that is never sent is a default nobody chose

nodes.label: Fault 20: A diagnostic tool with the fault it diagnoses

attributes.rationale: tools/scpi_console.py decided which lines produce a reply by looking for '?', but TSP has no query punctuation - a 2600B answers when the script calls print() - so every print(...) was sent as a write, the reply sat in the output buffer, and the next real query read the previous line's answer. Tools that produce evidence need the same scrutiny as the code they produce evidence about, because a wrong diagnostic's output is treated as a measurement. Prevention is to decide read-versus-write from the dialect, not from the text of the command: punctuation is not a protocol.

nodes.label: Windows/Ubuntu test matrix
nodes.rationale: Windows is the deployment platform and finds defects Linux structurally cannot; Ubuntu is fast and catches path-separator and case-sensitivity mistakes. One Python version, the one every machine runs; a newer one is added here first and must go green before requires-python and .python-version move.

nodes.label: _a_gui_test_never_reaches_a_real_dialog
nodes.rationale: A GUI test reached messagebox.showwarning unstubbed and the outcome depended on the machine: pumping that spanned the 10 ms timer opened a window that blocked forever, pumping that did not discarded the warning and passed - and the discarded message was the one telling an operator a sample may still be energised. Removing a stub now fails in about a second, naming the dialog.

nodes.label: run_tests.py --jobs split budget
nodes.rationale: The budget is split rather than shared because the two kinds of group behave in opposite ways: non-GUI files are CPU-bound and divide the work, while GUI files pump a Tk event loop and waiting does not divide, so they are capped at GUI_WORKERS. A single pool of twelve cost 7.4x the machine time to return 1.5x the wall clock, and took test_combined_window from 52 s to 455 s against a 600 s GROUP_TIMEOUT_S - a passing test one slower machine away from being reported as a hang.

nodes.label: bench_code driver staleness digest
nodes.rationale: Replaces a commit-date comparison, because a commit date is rewritten by git am, by a rebase and by a squash-merge, so the same bytes answered differently depending on when they were merged. Staleness compares a digest of the driver's contents plus its shared dependencies and consults no git at all. bench_result separately records a failure, since stale means nobody checked recently while failing means somebody did.

nodes.label: COMPLIANCE_READBACK_TRUSTED / RANGE_READBACK_TRUSTED flags
nodes.rationale: Three-valued: None means the driver answers and nobody has checked whether it tells the truth, because a readback an instrument answers dishonestly is worse than none. Every flag is a claim about a physical measurement, so none is set without a bench session. Confirmed on the 2401, 2611A, 2635B and B2901A; the GSM-20H10's range flag and the 2635B's power limit stay off.

nodes.label: Per-group timeout and pre-announcement in run_tests.py
nodes.norm_label: per-group timeout and pre-announcement in run_tests.py
nodes.rationale: A group was announced only once it had finished and print() to a pipe is block-buffered, so a run that never finished produced an empty log and ran toward the platform's six-hour default. Each group is now announced before it starts, killed past SMU_GROUP_TIMEOUT_S, and reported as TIMEOUT with whatever output it had, without stopping the groups after it.

nodes.label: smuniversal_lab_suite single installed namespace
nodes.rationale: core, devices, drivers and experiments used to install as four top-level packages plus a top-level `main` module - names at least as generic as the one the project had already refused to install and free to collide in a shared environment. The layout stays flat rather than src/, and docs name code by its path from the repository root except the driver/module fields and code fingerprint, which are package-relative so they mean the same files in a checkout and an installed copy.

nodes.label: Optional per-instrument extras
nodes.rationale: minismu, usb, direct-gpib and bench. `uv sync --extra bench` reproduces exactly what a plain `uv sync` installed before, so the bench workflow is one flag longer and nothing else; each extra has a named failure message and a test that provokes it.

nodes.label: One-way dependency: experiments to drivers to transports
nodes.norm_label: one-way dependency: experiments to drivers to transports
nodes.rationale: Nothing in core/ imports from experiments/, and no driver imports an experiment.

nodes.label: VISA stays the default GPIB path
nodes.norm_label: visa stays the default gpib path
nodes.rationale: pyvisa-py covers TCP and serial; the direct NI GPIB-HS transport is opt-in for machines that deliberately have no NI software, never a silent VISA fallback, and carries a Windows WinUSB prerequisite of its own.

nodes.label: Full-history checkout for the docs test
nodes.norm_label: full-history checkout for the docs test
nodes.rationale: tests/test_docs.py compares each driver against `git log -1 -- <driver>`, and a shallow clone reports HEAD for every tracked file. The test skips itself rather than lying when history is truncated, so fetch-depth: 0 is what stops it skipping in the one place it must run.

nodes.label: Liveness timeout bound on CI jobs
nodes.norm_label: liveness timeout bound on ci jobs
nodes.rationale: A liveness bound, not a performance target. Reaching it means something stopped and the log names what; without it a hung job runs to the platform default of six hours and reports a cancellation that says nothing. PYTHONUNBUFFERED is set for the same reason - print() to a pipe is block-buffered and a whole run's output fits in one buffer, so a step that never exits would produce an empty log.

nodes.label: Tkinter smoke check before anything else
nodes.norm_label: tkinter smoke check before anything else
nodes.rationale: A bare create/destroy/create smoke test so a broken Tcl/Tk shows up as its own failing step rather than as a puzzling test failure later. Interpreter comes from python.org/actions builds, not uv's managed distribution, because isolating the interpreter source is the point.

nodes.label: The commissioning round as a procedure
nodes.norm_label: the commissioning round as a procedure
nodes.rationale: Every instrument is checked in one pass rather than repaired one at a time, so a whole-fleet fingerprint is established at one commit and a fault common to the fleet is visible. The 2026-09-14 round ran seven instruments with seven passes; raising the GSM's read budget was deliberately declined because editing a driver would invalidate the fingerprint the round had just established.

nodes.label: timing marker for upper-bound tests
nodes.rationale: Tests asserting an upper bound on elapsed time are deselected from the parallel phase and run afterwards alone, because `elapsed < 0.26` is a claim about the machine as much as about the code and contention has twice sent someone to investigate a result that meant nothing. Lower bounds are not marked - contention can only make those more true.

nodes.label: run_tests.py --all is the only accepted green evidence
nodes.norm_label: run_tests.py --all is the only accepted green evidence
nodes.rationale: Plain pytest on a single file is fine while developing that file but is not a substitute for the runner, which gives each GUI file its own process. Ruff and mypy run alongside and are green on the tree today, which is what makes them enforceable.

nodes.label: core.checkup package, one module per tier
nodes.norm_label: core.checkup package, one module per tier
nodes.rationale: A 2,261-line module split into probes, base, tier1/tier2/tier3 mixins on Checkup, and report. Every name stays importable from core.checkup and no behaviour changed; the checkup's tests, its all-driver run and a demo checkup are the evidence.

nodes.label: core/clamping.py compliance_suspected detection
nodes.rationale: Checks readings for values at 98% of applied compliance, or three or more stuck at one value while the setpoint changed. It reads the data rather than the instrument's flag, so it works on instruments with no compliance flag.

nodes.label: core/readback.py five-state setting answer
nodes.rationale: A setting is a request until something reads it back: a refused setting raises nothing on any instrument here, so a successful write is evidence the link works and nothing else. States are unsupported, unreadable, unverified, confirmed, mismatched; only confirmed renders as a pass, and a mismatched is a failure whether or not the readback is verified. Unrecognised queries stay `unsupported` because an unanswered query times out and latches the transport.

nodes.label: ended_by: how a run finished
nodes.rationale: duration, operator or read_error. A trace that stops early looks identical to a complete one on a plot, so the column has to be checked before concluding anything from the length of a run.

nodes.label: Compliance is the setting that ruins data
nodes.norm_label: compliance is the setting that ruins data
nodes.rationale: A ceiling on the quantity you are not forcing. Set too low the curve stops being an I-V curve and becomes a picture of the limit; set at the instrument's maximum a shorted sample takes the full current. Most instruments here cannot report a trip, so a flat top on a curve may be the only warning you get.

nodes.label: GSM-20H10 measured on the old compliance's range
nodes.norm_label: gsm-20h10 measured on the old compliance's range
nodes.rationale: A wider measurement range was refused against the compliance *RST left and nothing re-sent it, so any run whose compliance was higher than the one already set ranged against the old compliance. Readings above ~105 uA overranged into a sentinel and were dropped, so the sweep came back short rather than wrong; a sweep staying under 105 uA is complete but was measured on a narrower range than its `ranges` column records. Fixed in the driver 2026-09-16.

nodes.label: 2401 turns its output off on a source-function change
nodes.norm_label: 2401 turns its output off on a source-function change
nodes.rationale: The driver disables auto output-off so a sweep holds its level between points, which means the output must be turned on after changing mode. Code that does not blocks forever on the next reading with no error, and the instrument looks dead.

nodes.label: miniSMU folds back to 50 mA on USB-C power
nodes.norm_label: minismu folds back to 50 ma on usb-c power
nodes.rationale: The declared 180 mA per channel needs the 12 V adapter, and there is no command that reports which supply is connected, so the software assumes the adapter and says so on every connect. On bus power a sweep asking for more folds back silently and the curve looks like a sample going into a compliance nobody set - if a run flattens at about 50 mA, check the barrel jack before the sample.

nodes.label: Tier 1 probe levels row states what was sourced
nodes.norm_label: tier 1 probe levels row states what was sourced
nodes.rationale: A module-wide PROBE_CURRENT of 1e-6 is a seventh of a count on the U2722A, so the tool was structurally unable to pass on a working instrument. Nominal levels are clamped into each model's declared envelope and the driver is asked for its floor on the range that is now active; the row is rewritten at the end of the run and the 'nothing moved' sentence is generated rather than stored so it cannot outlive the event that falsifies it.

nodes.label: stopped_early reaches the JSON report
nodes.rationale: It reached the Markdown banner and not the JSON, so three aborted GSM runs arrived as sheets of passes with nothing failed. The JSON is the half that gets sent to someone else, so it has to be readable on its own.

nodes.label: TransportDesynchronised latch
nodes.rationale: A query whose reply never arrives latches the transport into a refusing state until reconnect. There is no recovery: no later reply can be matched to the question that asked for it. write() stays permitted because a write never reads, which is what lets a poisoned session run output_off() and de-energise its sample. Clearing the latch is an explicit _begin_session() called only from connect(), after a device clear was found to silently un-desynchronise a poisoned session.

nodes.label: Fixed sourcing vs time
nodes.rationale: A new experiment with no original script, and one that has never been run against hardware - everything documented is verified against the simulated instrument and the test suite. The first bench session is expected to find something, because commissioning a new path always has.

nodes.label: Keithley 2401
nodes.rationale: 21 V, 1.05 A, software-stepped sweeps, general-purpose IV work up to 21 V. Carries the same compliance-ranging defect as the GSM (fixed 2026-09-16), and any low-bias data from the old script is suspect because source levels were rounded to four decimal places, quantising to 100 uV - at 100 uV a 21-point sweep collapses to three distinct levels while the file still lists 21.

nodes.label: Finish and save versus Stop and discard
nodes.norm_label: finish and save versus stop and discard
nodes.rationale: On every other tab Stop discards, which is deliberate and unchanged - and is why the button that keeps your data is called something else. The turn-on transient is deliberately inside the data: t = 0 is the output-on instant with no settle before the first sample.

nodes.label: The time column is what happened, not what was asked for
nodes.norm_label: the time column is what happened, not what was asked for
nodes.rationale: Gaps in time_s say the instrument could not keep up, and interval_achieved_s says it more compactly; compare against interval_requested_s before trusting any derived rate. A blank reading is a blank cell and never a missing row, so sample indices stay contiguous and a gap is visible rather than closing up and shifting everything after it earlier in time.

nodes.label: A run bounded by a timer is a safety property
nodes.norm_label: a run bounded by a timer is a safety property
nodes.rationale: Fixed sourcing vs time is bounded by real elapsed time so that nobody walks away from a live fixture.

nodes.label: Check the sensing column on old single sweeps
nodes.norm_label: check the sensing column on old single sweeps
nodes.rationale: The original only set 4-wire inside the periodic path, so a single sweep used whatever state the instrument was last left in - the same sample measured before and after a periodic run could differ with nothing recorded to say why.

nodes.label: Geometry correction factor substitution is flagged
nodes.norm_label: geometry correction factor substitution is flagged
nodes.rationale: A sample too small for the geometry table used to be silently over-reported, because the original substituted a correction factor of 1.0 - which means 'effectively infinite sample', the opposite of the truth for a small coupon. The substitution still happens but is flagged beside the result. Probe spacing is not adjustable because the correction tables are indexed in units of it, so a different probe head is a different set of tables.

nodes.label: Per-current resistance spread check
nodes.rationale: Each reading carries its own resistance_at_point_ohm and a spread above 2% is flagged; that usually means self-heating or non-ohmic contacts and is invisible in a single slope fitted across all currents, where R-squared can look excellent while the sample's resistance drifts with drive level.

nodes.label: 2-wire measures your cables as well as your sample
nodes.norm_label: 2-wire measures your cables as well as your sample
nodes.rationale: Use 4-wire below about 100 Ohm. On a 10 kOhm resistor the bench comparison gave 9948.76 Ohm 2-wire against 9951.87 Ohm 4-wire - 0.03%, invisible - but the scatter was fifty times lower in 4-wire (R-squared 0.999958 to 0.9999992), so it is worth using even where the mean agrees.

nodes.label: Settling: the instrument is not the slow part
nodes.norm_label: settling: the instrument is not the slow part
nodes.rationale: After the source changes the sample and cables take time to reach the new level, so reading too early measures the transition. Matters most for high-resistance samples, small currents (the U2722A slews at about 1 V/s sourcing 1 uA) and long or coaxial leads; the symptom is each point resembling the one before.

nodes.label: Source mode: force one quantity, measure the other
nodes.norm_label: source mode: force one quantity, measure the other
nodes.rationale: Force voltage on anything that might short, because a shorted sample with a forced current has nowhere to put it and the voltage runs to the compliance limit. Force current on anything high-resistance and for 4PP, Van der Pauw and Hall, which measure a voltage difference so the current has to be the known quantity.

nodes.label: U2722A settling, output capacitance and residue
nodes.norm_label: u2722a settling, output capacitance and residue
nodes.rationale: Stepped from -100 uA to +100 uA into 10 kOhm and read at once it read 71% of the step, taking about 0.3 s to come within 1%. With bare terminals the output looks like about 36 pF, so at 100 nA it ramps a volt per second and charge survives between runs - an early reading is the previous measurement's residue. The output is also down for about 228 ms across a source-function change, an order of magnitude longer than the Keithleys.

nodes.label: IV sweep (bench note)
nodes.rationale: Ported from the 2611A IV scripts. Old sweeps may hold fewer points than they claim or the wrong x-axis: the originals waited a rounded number of seconds then read the buffer regardless, and rebuilt the x-axis from requested levels rather than asking what was sourced. Neither is recoverable from an old file.

nodes.label: Ossila four-point probe (bench note)
nodes.rationale: Ported from Ossila_4PP_2611A.py and a triangular-sine variant. Old saved files differ by 1000x on the resistivity column - the original multiplied sheet resistance by a thickness in millimetres and labelled it mOhm/m - while sheet resistance and conductivity in those files are unchanged and correct. A sample thicker than twice the probe spacing used to crash.

nodes.label: Getting good measurements
nodes.rationale: You do not need to know how an SMU works internally, but five settings decide whether your numbers are right and all five are settings you choose.

nodes.label: Keysight U2722A
nodes.rationale: 20 V, 120 mA, 14-bit (range / 16384 whatever the NPLC), permanently 4-wire by wiring so the sensing control is greyed out and the CSV records '4-wire (hardwired)'. Every reading costs two integrations because there is no combined voltage+current read, so NPLC 25 is about 1.06 s per point and a 200-point sweep takes roughly 3.5 minutes. If it goes missing from the address dropdown, pick VISA (pyvisa-py) - it has a history of being opened by a vendor backend and then misbehaving.

nodes.label: The linear fit is optional and off for anything non-ohmic
nodes.norm_label: the linear fit is optional and off for anything non-ohmic
nodes.rationale: A diode will happily return a slope with a convincing R-squared, and that number is not a resistance.

nodes.label: Run the checkup before trusting an instrument
nodes.norm_label: run the checkup before trusting an instrument
nodes.rationale: Three minutes with nothing connected to the outputs, and it writes a report comparable against a previous one. Half the faults this project has found were found this way, and none of them could have been found by any amount of testing without an instrument attached.

nodes.label: Wrong data that looks right
nodes.rationale: Four real faults - a sweep of the right length all at 0 V, a sweep silently decimated to a third of its points, a sweep clipped by a range that never widened, and voltage and current for one point measured half a second apart - share one shape: none of them raised an error. Be suspicious of a very good fit, because clipped or decimated data has less of the sample's own scatter in it.

nodes.label: Measure a known resistor before trusting a session
nodes.norm_label: measure a known resistor before trusting a session
nodes.rationale: A 10 kOhm resistor takes two minutes and tests the whole chain - instrument, wiring, driver, analysis. Every fault this project has found produced data that looked entirely reasonable against an unknown sample and was obvious against a known one.

nodes.label: A retracted hypothesis never appears
nodes.rationale: Read back cold, an account of a wrong mechanism is indistinguishable from a finding, and this file has misled its own authors that way.

nodes.label: The Verified column
nodes.rationale: fails means the driver was run against the instrument and did not pass; re-check means the driver has been modified since it last met hardware; never means it has never met hardware at all; no access means the instrument cannot be reached, so no run is pending and none is coming.

nodes.label: GSM-20H10 hardware sweep appended an earlier sweep's tail
nodes.norm_label: gsm-20h10 hardware sweep appended an earlier sweep's tail
nodes.rationale: A shorter sweep than one taken earlier since power-up came back with the longer sweep's tail appended - plausible readings at levels the sample was never taken to, in the same file. Each IV run records points_requested, and the points past it are the old ones. Its buffer also returns three numbers per reading (voltage, current, resistance) regardless of being told otherwise. Fixed in the driver 2026-09-16.

nodes.label: B2901A energises its own output out of reset
nodes.norm_label: b2901a energises its own output out of reset
nodes.rationale: The B2900 series turns the output on by itself on a measurement trigger, so the driver sends :OUTP:ON:AUTO 0 on every reset and any hand-written script must do the same first.

nodes.label: B2901A compliance is sense-side
nodes.rationale: :SENS:CURR:PROT, where a 2450 uses a source limit. Send the Keithley spelling and the B2901A logs it, ignores it, and leaves the compliance at its reset value - and a sweep that then clamps still draws a convincing straight line.

nodes.label: bench_access / 'no access' instrument status
nodes.rationale: The Keithley 2450 sat in checkup-owed.md as the oldest unattended item on a list it does not belong on, because there is no access to a 2450 at all. bench_status() returns `unavailable` and the chooser marks it `no access`, so pending work is not confused with work that is never coming.

nodes.label: Choosing an SMU
nodes.rationale: Every number comes from the driver's own declarations, so the table cannot disagree with the software.

nodes.label: GW Instek GSM-20H10
nodes.rationale: 210 V, 1.05 A, sweeps on the instrument, 2- or 4-wire, reports compliance. The instrument to reach for when you need to know whether you hit compliance, and for long unattended sweeps of 2500 points on its own timebase.

nodes.label: Keithley 2450
nodes.rationale: No access: it is not in this lab and the hardware belongs to another group, so nothing has been confirmed at a bench and nothing is waiting on a session that is going to happen. Kept so the lab that owns one can adopt the suite. Every other driver was commissioned against real hardware and that process found nine faults, four of which produced plausible-looking wrong data rather than an error; there is no reason to think this driver is the exception, it simply has not been asked. Its *IDN? reply has never been read off a unit, so MODEL_IDS is written from the family convention and auto-detection may fail on first connect.

nodes.label: Keysight B2901A
nodes.rationale: 210 V, 3.03 A, the shortest aperture in the fleet at NPLC 0.0004, and the only instrument here above 1 A. The second-best choice after the GSM for compliance-critical work. It resets to 2-wire, worth naming because it is the newest driver and the least exercised. Van der Pauw or Hall results from before 13 August 2026 carry no compliance warning even if the instrument was limiting, because the flag asked about the wrong quantity whenever current was being sourced.

nodes.label: At the bench (index)
nodes.rationale: For anyone taking a measurement: no knowledge of how the software works is assumed and nothing here requires reading the code.

nodes.label: Generated bench pages are built from docs/ notes
nodes.norm_label: generated bench pages are built from docs/ notes
nodes.rationale: choosing-an-smu.md and everything under instruments/ and experiments/ is built from the developer notes in docs/ so the two cannot drift apart; editing them is pointless because the next build overwrites them and the test suite fails first.

nodes.label: One trip-axis rule for the SCPI drivers
nodes.norm_label: one trip-axis rule for the scpi drivers
nodes.rationale: The compliance trip is always on the quantity you are not sourcing, so the axis to query depends on the source function. OR-ing both trips adds a failure rather than removing one: a stale value on the unused axis reads as a clamp that is not happening. The B2901A's equivalent stays a separate implementation because that one is confirmed against hardware.

nodes.label: README routes and holds no reference material
nodes.norm_label: readme routes and holds no reference material
nodes.rationale: A landing page that also explains the instruments is a landing page that disagrees with the instrument notes within a month.

nodes.label: Stale driver versus unverified driver
nodes.rationale: Stale means checked once against its instrument but the code has moved since; unverified means it has never met the instrument at all. Those are different risks and prose that flattens them into 'not commissioned' is worse than no prose.

nodes.label: tools/bench_envelope.py noise/rate envelope
nodes.rationale: Reports achieved sample rate and relative standard deviation of a burst at each NPLC rung, discarding the first reading. RSD rather than peak-to-peak, which is set by the single worst sample and grows with burst length. Nothing is predicted from the load resistance: it was measured with one of these instruments, so using it to judge them is circular. The reading noise is the detection limit and is not the source floor.

nodes.label: The 200 V range needs the interlock line held high
nodes.norm_label: the 200 v range needs the interlock line held high
nodes.rationale: A physical line on the Digital I/O port that no command overrides: the output will not turn on above ~20 V without it, and a fixture lid opening takes the output off and keeps it off. On this bench the interlock is jumpered permanently, so the lid-open cutout the manual assumes is not in circuit and 200 V at up to 100 mA can stay live on an open fixture. The manual notes the line's reliability degrades after roughly 10,000 operations, which a permanent jumper never exercises, so if the wire is ever removed do not assume the line still works.

nodes.label: 2611A six-significant-figure readings before 11 August 2026
nodes.rationale: Six figures is about five parts per million, which is irrelevant for sheet resistance, IV sweeps and 4PP but matters for Hall, where the voltage is recovered by subtracting two nearly-equal readings so the precision of the difference is much worse than either reading. At a raw reading near 1 V, six figures means steps of about 10 uV, which can be larger than the Hall voltage being measured.

nodes.label: MEASURE_LOW_RANGE_FLOOR_A
nodes.rationale: Readings take about 87 ms and that is the price of the 100 pA range, because autoranging is allowed all the way down and searching those bottom decades is where the time goes. Raising the floor does not stop you reading sub-nanoamp currents - 10 pA still resolves on the 1 nA range - it stops autoranging onto the 100 pA range where the noise floor and accuracy are better below roughly 100 pA. Whether that matters is a property of your sample, so the constant must be changed deliberately and noted in the run: it changes what the instrument is capable of measuring, not just how fast.

nodes.label: U2722A: the range you land on changes the level you get
nodes.norm_label: u2722a: the range you land on changes the level you get
nodes.rationale: The same 0.1 V command came back as 0.1062 V on R20V and 0.1003 V on the finer range - 6% apart in one run on one instrument - because R20V's count is 1.2207 mV so 0.1 V rounds to 87 counts. There is no autorange here, so an axis left on AUTO takes the widest range and pays that quantisation; if a level has to be accurate, pin the range.

nodes.label: U2722A source floors and unreliable polarity
nodes.norm_label: u2722a source floors and unreliable polarity
nodes.rationale: Nothing below 1.22 mV on any range and nothing below 610 pA: below ten counts the output is offset rather than signal and its sign is not the one you asked for - the bench watched -1 uA and +1 uA produce the same output. A little above the floors the sign is still not guaranteed, because the zero offset drifts and has sat on both sides across three runs, so for reliable polarity stay above about three times the worst offset seen (roughly 0.25 uA on the 100 uA range, 5 mV on the 2 V range).

nodes.label: RangePlan NOT_SOURCED sentinel
nodes.rationale: RangePlan.for_sourcing() used to put AUTO on the axis of the quantity a run is not sourcing, but AUTO asks the instrument to choose a range while the intent was 'nothing is coming out of this axis'. BaseSMU._render_not_sourced turns it back into AUTO by default so commissioned instruments keep their behaviour, and renders_not_sourced records which drivers were verified. A U2722A override that passed its tests was removed once mutation showed it unreachable: a hook that looks load-bearing and never runs is worse than no hook.

nodes.label: Sub-count source floor
nodes.rationale: Below a count there is no signal, only offset residue, and its polarity is not commanded. Declared floors are refusal thresholds rather than converter widths: the crossing a halving walk finds follows each instrument's zero offset, which drifts between sessions, and a halving walk makes every level the range over a power of two, so matching a power-of-two count proves nothing. Sub-count behaviour is declared per axis as refused, unmeasured or not applicable, and the checkup warns on each unmeasured axis rather than passing over it.

nodes.label: BaseSMU.ZERO_RESIDUE_FRACTION
nodes.rationale: Sweep levels are computed, so for many ordinary point counts the level that should be zero comes out as about 1e-20 - a -100 uA to +100 uA sweep in 201 points put -1.36e-20 A at its midpoint - and a sub-count floor that exempted only an exact zero ended the run there. A level more than a million times below the floor is now treated as the zero it was meant to be, on both refusal paths.

nodes.label: app.check_source_point() refuses rather than clips
nodes.rationale: Nothing in the suite clips an out-of-range request: the operating point is validated against the connected driver's declared limits including a power envelope and refused outright, and range dropdowns are repopulated from the instrument on connect so unreachable values are never offered. A wrong LIMITS therefore matters.

nodes.label: Output off does not disconnect the sample
nodes.norm_label: output off does not disconnect the sample
nodes.rationale: By default the instrument sources 0 V into the sample rather than opening the output relay, because the relay has a finite number of operations in it. The High-Z option is what opens it.

nodes.label: Keithley 2611A
nodes.rationale: 200 V, 1.5 A, hardware sweeps, resolution not range-limited. The best instrument here when V and I must describe the same instant - one matched conversion, which matters most for Hall. A slow first point is not a fault: after any configuration change the first reading takes three integration periods rather than one.

nodes.label: Keithley 2635B
nodes.rationale: 200 V, 1.5 A, measures to 100 pA but sources only to 1 nA. The instrument for high-resistance samples, and that 100 pA range is the reason it is on the bench. The app's range dropdowns are fed from one list driving sourced levels and compliance, so the 100 pA measure range is not reachable from the app. Output off drives 0 V with 1 mA available, which on a high-resistance sample is six to nine orders of magnitude above what you are measuring.

nodes.label: Ten-count refusal threshold on the U2722A
nodes.norm_label: ten-count refusal threshold on the u2722a
nodes.rationale: Ten counts is a decision: one count is where a request first means anything and the error there is 100%; ten caps it at 10%. It costs something real - nothing below 1.22 mV can be sourced on any range.

nodes.label: record_id is per stored run, run_id is per lifecycle run
nodes.norm_label: record_id is per stored run, run_id is per lifecycle run
nodes.rationale: A periodic IV run commits several records sharing one run_id, so de-duplicating on run_id would delete real cycles. De-duplicate on record_id.

nodes.label: Stored-file schema (FILE_SCHEMA)
nodes.rationale: The schema integer in the # header of every CSV the suite writes, from core.run_store.FILE_SCHEMA. One integer for every file kind rather than one each, because two schemes need somebody to remember which is which and the version exists precisely for a reader who was not here. Versions 1 (record_id and header keys), 2 (build_id, additive), 3 (no column name written twice; compliance_tripped renamed).

nodes.label: Method versions made load-bearing by golden files
nodes.norm_label: method versions made load-bearing by golden files
nodes.rationale: Versions live in core.calculation.METHODS and tests/golden/*.json is what makes them load-bearing: change a formula without bumping its version and the golden file stops reproducing. A new method with neither golden cases nor a written reason in NOT_YET_COVERED fails the suite.

nodes.label: bench_code is content, not a date
nodes.norm_label: bench_code is content, not a date
nodes.rationale: A commit date is not a property of the tree: git am, rebase and GitHub squash-merge all rewrite it, so the same bytes answered differently and a merge turned main red with nothing in the tree changed. bench_code is a 12-char digest of the driver plus its shared dependencies from core.provenance.code_fingerprint, printed in every checkup report header; it survives rebases and needs no git, working on a zip download. It over-reports (a comment-only edit marks the driver stale) in the same conservative direction the date rule had.

nodes.label: bench_revalidated is the escape hatch and costs a sentence
nodes.norm_label: bench_revalidated is the escape hatch and costs a sentence
nodes.rationale: The staleness check deliberately over-reports: a docstring edit to base_instrument.py or base_smu.py marks the whole fleet stale because the check cannot tell a comment from a command. Both are named in core.provenance.SHARED_CODE_PATHS and tests/test_instrument_contract.py fails if a base is left out. A bare true is refused — the test requires prose naming the commit and why it does not affect what the checkup proved, because waving a driver through should cost a sentence, not a keystroke.

nodes.label: build_id, because a release number that never moves says nothing
nodes.norm_label: build_id, because a release number that never moves says nothing
nodes.rationale: app_version is set by hand and said 0.1.0 from Wave 7b-ii through every behaviour-changing wave, so files months apart answered 'which code produced this?' identically. build_id welds the commit on in three forms — clean, .dirty (the code that ran exists nowhere else), and +unknown. Twelve hex characters, the same width core.provenance prints, so a stored file and a bench report compare by eye. unknown is written rather than the key omitted, because an absent key reads as 'written by a version that did not record builds' while unknown reads as 'tried and could not tell'. A frozen .exe reads a baked-in constant.

nodes.label: Identifier shape and the width of the random tail
nodes.norm_label: identifier shape and the width of the random tail
nodes.rationale: The tail was 32 bits on the strength of an arithmetic claim in core/identity.py of a collision 'roughly every ten thousand years'; the birthday expectation for 300 draws from 2^32 is about 1.0e-5 per day, i.e. one collision every ~260 years, and a rec- is minted per run. At 64 bits the figure is ~10^12 years. The session component on a run identifier is 64 bits drawn once per process, because without it a restarted application or a second bench machine produced the identical first run identifier — and run_id is the join key between a stored row and the event log, so that collision joined one run's readings to another run's outcome. parse_object_id and parse_run_id still accept the old shapes; only the new one is written.

nodes.label: Line endings: LF, decided
nodes.rationale: Identical code produced LF on Linux and CRLF on Windows: run_store.py sets lineterminator="\n" while LabApp.write_atomic() opened in text mode and translated every one, so the builder and the file on disk disagreed. RFC 4180 specifies CRLF so that was defensible too — what was not defensible is that neither end had decided. Settled as LF because a file whose bytes depend on which bench machine saved it cannot be compared or checksummed, and csv, pandas.read_csv and Excel all read either. Not a schema version, and nothing already written needs converting.

nodes.label: Rule 3: Results and saving — no auto-save, ever
nodes.norm_label: rule 3: results and saving — no auto-save, ever
nodes.rationale: A run spoiled by a misaligned sample or a badly seated contact must be discardable without ever leaving a file behind. _record_run registers the run under the same Treeview item id as its table row, so a row and its raw data cannot drift apart. Known cost accepted deliberately: an unsaved run exists only in memory, so a crash loses it; the fix on offer if it ever bites is a quiet session-recovery file deleted on successful save.

nodes.label: Saving is a snapshot, and the button says so
nodes.norm_label: saving is a snapshot, and the button says so
nodes.rationale: A save writes everything in the store and leaves it there, so pressing Save twice writes earlier runs again. The overlap is the design, usable only because the files admit it: save_kind: snapshot, a save_id shared by one press's files, and a record_id per row, so combining is drop_duplicates(subset="record_id"). Option B — export only new runs — was rejected because the # header holds calculated results derived from every run in the store, so a new-runs-only file would carry a sheet resistance computed from readings that file does not contain: a correct-looking number above a table that cannot produce it. Calculated results attach only to the sample currently named, because copying them onto every sample would invent results for samples never calculated.

nodes.label: Rule 10: A derived value carries its provenance
nodes.norm_label: rule 10: a derived value carries its provenance
nodes.rationale: Physical quantities go through core/calculation.py rather than reading widget strings and writing label strings: build a CalculationInput on the main thread, validate(), require_set() where inputs must be complete, derive() to a frozen DerivedResult. Three rules learned the hard way — provenance is all-or-nothing per run because a chain that is half true reads exactly like one that is whole; the staleness signature must include every input the result depends on, not just the numbers (Hall's sample_type changes reported carrier density by a factor of thickness while moving none of the eight voltages); and calculated_fields() returns {} when stale, because the grey text on the panel is advice while this is the part that cannot be ignored. Raw data still saves.

nodes.label: Rule 11: The per-sample summary, and its one overwrite
nodes.norm_label: rule 11: the per-sample summary, and its one overwrite
nodes.rationale: The app writes the summary from each experiment's SUMMARY_QUANTITIES declaration, same capability pattern as provide(), because the app must not know the shape of any experiment's result. A per-experiment writer was rejected: it would produce two half-summaries, one clobbering the other, because each tab saves separately. A missing half is a written 'not calculated' row rather than a gap, so a part-finished sample cannot read as a fully measured one. Staleness is inherited for free through calculated_fields(). A PermissionError is swallowed to a logged warning — the summary is written after the data CSVs and outside their try, so a summary open in Excel on Windows must not turn a good save into a reported failure.

nodes.label: The summary's one overwrite, decided at first run
nodes.norm_label: the summary's one overwrite, decided at first run
nodes.rationale: Data CSVs auto-suffix through unique_filename and cannot be lost; the summary is derived from files still on disk, so it alone may replace itself. summary_collision_decision fires at the first run rather than the first save, because by save time the runs already carry the identity they were measured under and the check's real value is the early 'you already have data under this name' warning before twenty minutes of measuring. Keyed by (sample, folder) and re-armed when either changes; note_sample_context_changed compares against the last pair it acted on because the sample-name trace fires even when the box is re-set to its current value — without that, a chosen overwrite silently turned back into a suffix before Save ran, a real trap found by mutation.

nodes.label: What the exception policy enforces, and what it cannot
nodes.norm_label: what the exception policy enforces, and what it cannot
nodes.rationale: tests/test_exception_policy.py checks only that a reason was written, not that it is true — no test can do the second. The point is that the reason becomes an artefact a reviewer can disagree with in the diff that introduces it, rather than a silence nobody can argue with three years later. The surface covers run control, the run store, the event log, provenance, identity, ownership, the app shell, the experiment base and the driver contract; drivers, transports, panels and tools are not on it yet, recorded as a per-area pass because writing 55 invariants in one change would produce 55 sentences nobody had time to mean. Ruff's S110 and S112 are deliberately not enabled: a linter sees the shape and not the path, so it would flag the correct after_cancel cleanup and the wrong shutdown identically, and a gate that fires 74 times on the day it is switched on teaches everybody to ignore it.

nodes.rationale: What a tool writes must be determined by the repository and by nothing else about the machine. ROOT.rglob('*.py') let a .uv-cache inside the checkout and agent worktrees under .claude/ feed a generated page from files no commit contains; owned_files() lists tracked files, with a filtered walk as the fallback where git cannot answer.

nodes.label: core/provenance.py commit, dirty flag and firmware
nodes.norm_label: core/provenance.py commit, dirty flag and firmware
nodes.rationale: Reports carry the commit they ran at, whether the tree was dirty, and the instrument's firmware from *IDN?, emitted into the JSON and the Markdown header from one call so the two cannot drift. Written from the real *IDN? replies rather than the SCPI standard, because two of them do not follow it. The dirty flag says what was dirty, because a flag that is sometimes alarming and sometimes not gets ignored - and the time it is ignored is the time it was real.

nodes.label: build_id stamped on every stored record
nodes.norm_label: build_id stamped on every stored record
nodes.rationale: The release with the commit welded on, `.dirty` on a modified tree, `+unknown` where no build can be determined. A frozen build reads a baked-in constant so correctness does not depend on git being on PATH, and `unknown` is written rather than the key omitted.

nodes.label: FILE_SCHEMA stored-file schema
nodes.rationale: Bumped to 3 when a Fixed source file was found to carry two columns named `compliance` - the run's limit and each sample's trip flag - so a reader keyed on names kept one and lost the other without an error. The flag is now compliance_tripped and build_sample_csv refuses a run key equal to a reading key.

nodes.label: 64-bit run identifiers with SESSION_ID
nodes.rationale: The 32-bit tail came from a docstring's arithmetic wrong by a factor of forty; a restart inside one second or a second bench machine produced the identical first run identifier, and run_id is the join key between stored rows and the event log.

nodes.label: LF newlines decided for generated and stored files
nodes.norm_label: lf newlines decided for generated and stored files
nodes.rationale: Generated pages were written with CRLF on Windows and staleness was judged with read_text, which decodes both forms identically, so every --check that should have caught it passed. Writes go through write_lf and staleness is judged on bytes; measurement CSVs had the same disagreement between a builder's lineterminator and write_atomic().

nodes.label: The CSV plotter window
nodes.rationale: Identifies each file from its title, name and columns and reports when those disagree. It opens no instrument, so it takes no single-instance lock and runs beside a measurement window. Schema 2 files onwards.

nodes.label: Append-only changelog rule
nodes.rationale: An entry says what changed and why it matters - the conclusion - not how it was reached. Reasoning is put where it will be found again: instrument facts in docs/instruments/, mistakes in docs/faults/, design constraints in docs/architecture/ or docs/rules/. Anything surviving none of those tests was working material. Two deliberate condensation breaks (2026-08-27 and 2026-09-03) are recorded as exceptions.

nodes.label: One shape for every fault note
nodes.norm_label: one shape for every fault note
nodes.rationale: Symptom / Cause / Risk / Detection / Prevention / Status / Evidence, so two notes can be compared without reading both end to end. Detection and Prevention are separate because most of these faults were survivable once somebody knew to look, and the looking is the transferable part; Status exists because a note that does not say what is closed reads as closed.

nodes.label: Deleting the code review document
nodes.rationale: About 210 source comments cited a 1,953-line review as `review SN` or `group B3`, and for several modules that citation was the only recorded reason the module existed. Every one was replaced with the house rule, architecture page or fault note that actually holds the fact before the file was removed, and tests/test_docs.py refuses a new citation so one cannot come back pointing at nothing. Wave N framing left the comments too: a comment saying when something changed dates itself, one stating the invariant does not.

nodes.label: MAJOR.SESSION.PUSH version number
nodes.rationale: The number had stayed at 0.1.0 through every change since it was introduced; it now moves with every push so a stored record's app_version distinguishes builds.

nodes.label: HANDOFF.md carries no branch or wave state
nodes.norm_label: handoff.md carries no branch or wave state
nodes.rationale: It used to name the branch the current work was on, and by the time anyone read it that branch had been merged and deleted; two readers of two checkouts days apart reached opposite conclusions about which branches existed, one from remote-tracking refs no `git fetch --prune` had cleaned. The fix is to remove the dependency, not to update the value - branch state is not written down in this repository at all. The file is kept only because notes, commit messages and past conversations point at it by name.

nodes.norm_label: no auto-save: saving is a snapshot
nodes.rationale: Runs are not written to disk as they finish; nothing is saved until Save snapshot to CSV, so a spoiled run can be deleted without ever leaving a file behind.

nodes.label: Weekly dependency audit workflow
nodes.rationale: Scheduled weekly and deliberately not a PR gate: an advisory published today makes yesterday's green run wrong without anything in the repository changing, so blocking a merge would fail whoever opens the next PR for something they did not do and cannot fix in that branch - and the answer people reach for is to disable the check.

nodes.label: Lint and type gates job
nodes.rationale: Runs ruff and mypy in one cell rather than across the OS matrix: neither reads the operating system, and a finding repeated four times is still one finding.

nodes.label: experiments/four_contact.py shared base class
nodes.rationale: What Van der Pauw and Hall had copied from each other - instrument configuration before the output goes on, the pre-run refusals, thickness and voltage inputs, stage temperature and the results-table tick box - is one class. What differs (run sequence, polarity handling, calculation) stays in each experiment. The rest of the controller split is parked with a trigger: the first fix that has to be made in more than one controller.

nodes.label: core/gui/run_controls.py shared Run/Stop panel
nodes.rationale: Every experiment carried its own copy of the panel and of set_lamp, _enter_run_ui, _end_run and stop_pressed, identical but for comments and a 4PP lamp that had drifted to a different green. A tab with more buttons now lists them via _idle_only_buttons/_run_only_buttons instead of overriding handlers, and the shared _end_run tolerates only a widget destroyed by a closing window so faults surface.

nodes.label: Bounded on_close() shutdown sequence
nodes.rationale: An explicit bounded sequence - refuse new runs, cancel every controller, wait for idle while draining the UI queue, de-energise, disconnect, destroy - bounded by CLEANUP_TIMEOUT_S, with expiry naming the tab in a modal. LabApp cancels every controller directly so the guarantee does not depend on a subclass remembering super().

nodes.label: StageShutdownReport confirmed de-energise
nodes.rationale: The de-energise could not fail and could not have reported success if it had, because the stage firmware never acknowledges a command. confirm_pid_off() is now confirmed against a status line broadcast after the OFF, and anything else raises a modal naming the stage. The matching unsaved-measurement guard reported 'nothing to lose' when it broke, so unsaved_state() returns a count plus the experiments it could not read.

nodes.label: docs/open/technical-debt.md as a graded table
nodes.rationale: Graded by impact - safety, data, evidence, correctness, maintenance - because two dozen prose items of a page each is unprioritisable. It answers what is still wrong; the changelog answers the other question, so closed items are deleted rather than marked closed and left.

nodes.label: pip-audit against the locked environment
nodes.rationale: Audits uv.lock with all extras because uv.lock is what bench machines actually resolve; auditing pyproject's version ranges would audit versions nobody has installed. An advisory against a package only a bench machine installs is still an advisory against a bench machine.

nodes.label: Exceptions are not suppressed silently (house rule 13)
nodes.norm_label: exceptions are not suppressed silently (house rule 13)
nodes.rationale: Safety, data-preservation and provenance paths do not suppress. Ruff's S110 is deliberately not enabled because a linter sees the shape and not the path, so it flags a correct after_cancel cleanup and a wrong shutdown identically; tests/test_exception_policy.py checks over fourteen named modules that a reason was written, and no test can check that it is true.

nodes.label: A lint gate chosen to be green today
nodes.norm_label: a lint gate chosen to be green today
nodes.rationale: Ruff with every rule enabled reports about 12,800 findings here, and a job that starts 12,800 in the red is how a real failure gets waved through - so the criterion for enabling a rule was 'is it green on this tree today'. Two of the 93 findings fixed were real defects present since the first import: BaseSMU.measure() was not abstract and returned None, and FourPointProbeExperiment.delete_ticked() overrode the base without calling it.

nodes.label: mypy at the boundaries only
nodes.rationale: Seven files are checked: the transport protocol, the driver contract, run control, the parameter snapshots, the ranging plan, the per-model envelope and the readback answer. It found nplc, high_z, ovp and voltage_range_v declared as bare types with a None default, where None means 'leave the instrument alone' rather than 'send a default'.
