nodes.label: House rules index
nodes.rationale: Requirements every experiment meets, each asked for explicitly and not stylistic preferences to be re-litigated. The numbers are permanent because they are cited from source comments and past conversations — a rule is never renumbered, only the note explaining it moves, and a retired rule keeps its number and says it is retired.

nodes.label: The second reason run_tests.py is load-bearing
nodes.norm_label: the second reason run_tests.py is load-bearing
nodes.rationale: Beyond the Windows Tcl runtime, a platform-independent reason present now: many GUI test files monkeypatch base_experiment.messagebox and base_app.messagebox at import time over the same shared attribute, and pytest imports every module during collection, so the last file imported wins and earlier files assert against a recorder nothing writes to. Proved by import order, not inferred. The mechanism is loud in one direction and silent in the other — assertions of the ABSENCE of a dialog pass against a stolen empty recorder whether or not the code is correct. The sixteen errors under plain pytest are the canary; fixing them by relaxing assertions rather than isolating processes kills it.

nodes.label: Rule 1: Landscape three-column layout
nodes.rationale: Monitors are wide and short; before this was fixed Hall's window was 1333 x 1219, taller than a 1080p desktop, so the Run button sat below the bottom edge and nothing reported an error. Experiment.build_panels() builds three columns and must not be overridden — override on_panels_built() instead, because an override forgetting super() would silently produce no columns. A panel picks its column by the attribute it packs into, so there is no registry to keep in step. Spare width goes to col_right because the other two are fixed-content forms.

nodes.label: The pixel budget is a tripwire, not a guard
nodes.norm_label: the pixel budget is a tripwire, not a guard
nodes.rationale: Budget is <=1600 x 1000 px, aspect >=1.2, enforced by tests/test_layout.py — a new experiment must be added to its EXPERIMENTS list or it is not covered. Wave 5c added a reminder that passed on the development machine and failed Ubuntu CI at 1010 px because the runner's fonts are larger; on a slightly smaller font it would have reported nothing while the window grew. So the specific failure has a structural guard of its own, test_the_session_strip_stays_one_row_tall, which fails identically everywhere.

nodes.label: Rule 2: The console stays
nodes.rationale: core/gui/console_panel.py is built by LabApp for every experiment and must not be removed. It is collapsible via its checkbox, worth about 150 px on a short screen, and app.log() is safe from any thread because it goes through the UI queue.

nodes.label: Rule 4: The temperature stage is one line
nodes.norm_label: rule 4: the temperature stage is one line
nodes.rationale: build_temp_panel in PANELS is the whole wiring; self.temp_ctrl already exists and LabApp.shutdown_devices() — the window's, not the experiment's, because one window holds one stage — switches the PID off and closes the port, confirming the stage stopped rather than assuming a clean write meant it did. Temperature is recorded per run in metadata rather than in a file header: a header temperature describes the session, a row temperature describes the reading, and a run where the stage was still settling is only visible in the second form.

nodes.label: Rule 5: SI inside, convert only at the edges
nodes.norm_label: rule 5: si inside, convert only at the edges
nodes.rationale: Internals are SI base; every numeric parameter or result field names its unit (settle_s, thickness_m, field_t, compliance_v) with _n for dimensionless counts, which is an explicit statement that there is no unit rather than an omission that might mean anything. Conversion happens at the boundary in one named method on the parameter object, not inline at the call site. It earns a rule because the original Van der Pauw notebook mixed seconds and milliseconds in one settle delay and the 4PP original labelled Rs x t in millimetres as mOhm/m — neither raised anything. New parameter classes must be added to PARAMETER_CLASSES or they are not covered.

nodes.label: Rule 6: Operator input goes through core.validation
nodes.norm_label: rule 6: operator input goes through core.validation
nodes.rationale: int(float(text)) accepted 2.5 as 2 at five call sites, so a decimal in an integer box produced a different experiment from the one requested, silently. ValidationError subclasses ValueError so existing except ValueError handling already shows a dialog, and it carries .field so a panel can highlight the offending box. Scope is operator input only — the int(float(...)) calls in drivers parse SCPI error codes where truncation is the intended reading.

nodes.label: Rule 8: app.ui() is a queue, not a direct callback
nodes.norm_label: rule 8: app.ui() is a queue, not a direct callback
nodes.rationale: Workers never call into Tcl. This replaced a direct root.after(0, ...) from the worker, which is not thread-safe because after() registers a Tcl command and Tcl is single-threaded — the application only survived it because the main thread sits inside mainloop(). Tests driving the loop with root.update() must call drain_ui_now(): sixty back-to-back update() calls take well under one pump interval, so without the drain a committed row is still in the queue when assertions run. core/thread_guard.py is the opt-in diagnostic for 'is anything still reading Tk from a worker?', which is why nothing appears to call it.

nodes.label: Rule 9: Converted values are compared with a tolerance, never ==
nodes.norm_label: rule 9: converted values are compared with a tolerance, never ==
nodes.rationale: Measured, not assumed: on realistic typed values a round trip x/1e6 then *1e6 fails to return x for about 2.9% of entries, and x*1e-6 then *1e6 for 28.7%. core/units.py uses the better one and the residue is inherent — no arrangement of the arithmetic removes it. 180 um comes back as 179.99999999999997: scientifically irrelevant, legible enough to matter when someone opens the CSV. Use math.isclose on geometry values that have been through the snapshot.

nodes.label: Rule 13: A suppressed exception states the invariant that makes it safe
nodes.norm_label: rule 13: a suppressed exception states the invariant that makes it safe
nodes.rationale: Production code holds 169 except Exception handlers, 62 suppressing outright; most are correct. Review A-09 measured them because two of the project's worst faults had the same shape — fault 29 swallowed the stage's pid_off() and close() so a heater could stay enabled after the window closed, and fault 30's unsaved-measurement guard caught everything and returned a count, so a failure and a genuine all-clear were both 0 and the action taken on 0 was destructive. Neither was a missing handler; both were a handler that turned a failure into something indistinguishable from success. Safety, data-preservation and provenance paths do not suppress — they return a value the caller must branch on or raise, because 'nothing went wrong' and 'I could not tell' must not share a spelling. A cleanup-only suppression carries a comment stating not that it is safe but why. except: with no class is never correct because it swallows KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit.

nodes.label: R_fit_ohm recorded beside R(ave)
nodes.rationale: On an ohmic contact the two agree closely; a large gap between them on one position is worth a second look at that position's contacts.

nodes.label: miniSMU -1.5 mV voltage offset
nodes.rationale: Confirmed three ways. It cancels in anything taken from a slope - both 10 kOhm sweeps recovered the resistor to better than 0.1% - but not in a single-point voltage reading, which is what four-point-probe and Hall voltages are, and those are often smaller than the offset itself. It was -0.7 to -0.8 mV on 2026-09-11: the size moves between sessions and the sign has been negative every time.

nodes.label: Thickness in nanometres (thickness_nm)
nodes.rationale: Thickness takes a unit and a bare number is nanometres; files write thickness_nm instead of thickness_um. Typing 180 meaning micrometres now means nanometres.

nodes.label: Van der Pauw per-run line fit (R_fit_ohm)
nodes.norm_label: van der pauw per-run line fit (r_fit_ohm)
nodes.rationale: Slope is the run's resistance and intercept its offset voltage; fit_slope, fit_intercept, fit_r_squared and R_fit_ohm are written per run. R(ave) still feeds the calculation and which one should is to be decided from bench data.

nodes.label: vdp_hall: Van der Pauw and Hall share one window
nodes.norm_label: vdp_hall: van der pauw and hall share one window
nodes.rationale: A Van der Pauw run always immediately precedes a Hall measurement on the same mounted sample with the same contacts, so the two share one SMU connection, sample name and thickness, temperature stage and save folder. Hall is not offered on its own, because a Hall window that cannot obtain a sheet resistance is a trap rather than a choice.

nodes.label: Hall effect (bench note)
nodes.rationale: Ported from Hall_v4.ipynb. Results from before August 2026 carry two independent six-significant-figure precision floors, one in the software and one in the instrument; because the Hall voltage is a small difference between large readings that is roughly a 0.1% floor on V_H and everything derived from it, so noisy or irreproducible old Hall numbers are more likely to be this than the sample.

nodes.label: Van der Pauw (bench note)
nodes.rationale: Ported from the VdP notebooks. Sheet resistance is computed from eight readings, not two, and a run reporting fewer is refused rather than computed from what arrived. Voltages are recorded to nine significant figures rather than six; results from the original notebook carry a precision floor of about 0.1% on anything derived from a difference of two readings.

nodes.label: Per-tab Equations window
nodes.rationale: Formulas live in each experiment's math module beside the functions that evaluate them, and tests/test_equations.py holds them in step with core.calculation.METHODS. Numbers are withheld while a result is stale, as they are from the saved file.

nodes.label: Carrier type as a sign sanity check
nodes.norm_label: carrier type as a sign sanity check
nodes.rationale: Carrier type comes from the sign of the Hall voltage, and a sign flip is what a swapped pair of contacts looks like - the cheapest sanity check available on a Hall run.

nodes.label: Sheet resistance is handed over in memory, in one session
nodes.norm_label: sheet resistance is handed over in memory, in one session
nodes.rationale: The sheet resistance is carried in memory, not read from a file, so yesterday's Van der Pauw cannot feed today's Hall. Re-running takes minutes and measures the same contacts you are about to use.

nodes.label: Generated frontmatter fields from tools/build_docs.py
nodes.rationale: Everything between the markers is written from the driver class; hand-editing is pointless because the next build overwrites it and the test fails first. Paths are relative to smuniversal_lab_suite/ — the root the code fingerprint is computed against — so they name the same files in a checkout and an installed copy. compliance_trip is asked by comparing the driver's method against BaseSMU's stub rather than looking for the name, because a driver could define the method and still not implement it.

nodes.label: Note frontmatter schema
nodes.rationale: Not decoration: bench/choosing-an-smu.md and checkup-owed are built from it and tests/test_docs.py refuses a note missing a field. There are no defaults, because a default here is a claim nobody made — bench_ever defaulting to false would quietly mark a commissioned driver unverified, and defaulting to true would do the far worse opposite, which is exactly the mistake the old prose documents made.

nodes.label: Documentation migration status
nodes.rationale: Exists so nobody reads a stub and concludes the information was lost. The rebuild is finished across five patches; PORTING_NOTES.md, INSTRUMENTS.md, WAVE_PLAN.md and LAB54_DEVELOPMENT_REVIEW_AND_WORKFLOW.md are deleted, HANDOFF.md survives as a router, and the ~210 'review §N' citations were each replaced with the house rule, architecture page or fault note that holds the fact — tests/test_docs.py refuses a new one.

nodes.label: Transcribe manuals to Markdown rather than ship PDFs
nodes.norm_label: transcribe manuals to markdown rather than ship pdfs
nodes.rationale: A PDF cannot be grepped, diffed or linked to from a driver note, and the PDFs are not in the repository. The honest cost is that a hand-transcribed table can be transcribed wrong, so each is checked against the PDF once at the point of writing; a value that could not be read with confidence is recorded as unknown rather than guessed, the same rule the frontmatter applies to *IDN? strings.

nodes.label: Known-stale claims corrected on the way through
nodes.norm_label: known-stale claims corrected on the way through
nodes.rationale: Listed so corrections are visible as corrections rather than arriving silently inside a large move. Includes a fabricated *IDN? for the 2635B (real reply read off the unit 2026-08-13: Keithley Instruments Inc., Model 2635B, 4126721, 3.2.2), 'not yet commissioned' claims contradicted within their own sections, hardcoded counts now generated, and a Python floor stated as 3.12 where pyproject.toml requires >=3.14. The 3.12 floor's original reasoning — the Neumaier summation change — is still correct and worth recording even though the floor has moved past it.

nodes.label: One concern per patch
nodes.rationale: The skeleton adds capability nothing reads, so it cannot regress anything; the content patches then adopt it one layer at a time. Instrument and experiment material were split because their deviations come from different sources (command references vs original scripts) and one diff would mean a red test could not say which half caused it. Same shape as Waves 6d-i and 6d-ii, where the first changed no wire traffic at all — which is what made every existing test staying green mean something.

nodes.label: bench_access separates 'nobody has' from 'nobody can'
nodes.rationale: unverified used to cover both, so the 2450 sat in the checkup-owed to-do list as an item no amount of waiting would clear. The two look identical in a table and lead to different decisions, so bench_status() returns unavailable, the chooser marks 'no access', and the generated page drops advice nobody can act on. Hand-written, because whether a lab can reach a piece of hardware is not derivable from any file in the repository.

nodes.label: idn must be observed, never plausible
nodes.norm_label: idn must be observed, never plausible
nodes.rationale: If nobody has read the string off the unit, idn is null and idn_confirmed is false; a guess is refused by the test. INSTRUMENTS.md printed an invented serial, wrong capitalisation and wrong firmware for the 2635B inside a code block formatted identically to the real ones, with a caveat two lines below that a reader copying the string never sees.

nodes.label: The per-line lint-ok escape
nodes.rationale: Two tests/test_docs.py checks read prose: one refuses a hardcoded count of drivers, instruments, experiments or test files, one refuses a mention of a driver method Wave 6d-ii deleted. Both honour <!-- lint-ok --> per line, for sentences recording history rather than making a live claim. Deliberately not a file-level opt-out, which would be added once and silently inherited by everything written into that file afterwards.

nodes.label: The supported YAML subset
nodes.rationale: tools/build_docs.py parses this itself rather than depending on PyYAML: adding a dependency to read four kinds of scalar would put a third-party parser between the documentation and the test that guards it, and CI installs with uv sync --locked. Strings are always quoted because plain YAML scalars bite silently (a value beginning ~ reads as null, one containing ': ' reads as a mapping). Anything outside the subset raises rather than being skipped, because a hand-rolled parser that quietly mis-reads would put wrong numbers into generated pages with nothing to say so.

nodes.label: :SYSTem:ERRor query family (GSM-20H10)
nodes.rationale: FIFO queue of up to 10 messages, with [:NEXT]?, :ALL?, :COUNt? and the CODE variants. The manual does not say what [:NEXT]? returns on an empty queue; measured 2026-08-27 it returns 0,"No error" in about 8 ms, same as :ALL?.

nodes.label: :TRACe:FEED buffer source selection (GSM-20H10)
nodes.rationale: Selects whether raw SENSe readings or Calc1/Calc2 math results land in the buffer, and cannot be changed while buffer storage is active.

nodes.label: :TRACe:FEED? undocumented but answers
nodes.rationale: Undocumented but present, replying in about 10 ms. It is the only way to know what the buffer is actually storing: a buffer left on CALCulate1 returns math results where the suite expects raw readings — plausible numbers, wrong ones, with nothing in the data to say so, and any prior user of the instrument could have left it that way.

nodes.label: :INITiate[:IMMediate]
nodes.rationale: Takes the GSM out of idle; :READ? and :MEASure? also initiate. With auto output-off disabled the source must be turned on first, except for :MEASure? which turns it on automatically.

nodes.label: :OUTPut[:STATe] source on/off (GSM-20H10)
nodes.rationale: Measurements cannot be made while the source is off; turning it off places the GSM in the idle state unless source auto-clear is enabled. OUTP1 ON is rejected with -102 Syntax error, so the optional [1] suffix is not written that way.

nodes.label: :SOURce:CLEar:AUTO auto output-off
nodes.rationale: Enabled, the output turns on at the start of each SDM cycle and off after each measurement. Disabled — the *RST and :SYSTem:PRESet default — the output must already be on before :INITiate or :READ? can start, and it stays on after the instrument returns to idle, which the manual itself flags as a warning.

nodes.label: V1.16 rejects the manual's own SENSe1 token
nodes.norm_label: v1.16 rejects the manual's own sense1 token
nodes.rationale: Measured 2026-08-27: firmware V1.16 accepts SENS but answers -140 Character data error to SENSe1, SENS1, SENSE1 and RAW — including the exact token the manual gives as its example and the exact token TRAC:FEED? itself reports back. Not a general long-mnemonic problem, since CALCulate1 is accepted in full. SENS is the form that works. The divergence cost a bench session.

nodes.label: :OUTPut? does not report the truth
nodes.rationale: Measured 2026-08-20 with the output physically on and 10 V sourced from the front panel, both OUTP? and OUTP:STAT? returned 0 while READ? returned +9.999960e+00. Nothing in the suite queries it — the checkup infers output state from whether the write succeeded — and it should stay that way, because a query that lies is worse than no query.

nodes.label: NPLC trades noise against speed
nodes.rationale: Whole numbers of power line cycles matter because mains hum picked up on the leads averages to almost exactly zero over a whole cycle - which is why the window is measured in cycles rather than milliseconds, and why 1 NPLC is much quieter than 0.9. The U2722A pays twice (no combined voltage+current read) and the miniSMU's NPLC number is not a real integration time.

nodes.label: miniSMU compliance overshoots by about 2%
nodes.rationale: Measured 2026-09-04: a 1.0 V limit settled at -1.022 V into an open circuit, where every other instrument in that round held within 0.05% of its own limit. The clamp works and the checkup's ceiling is set clear of exactly this, but a limit set at the value your sample tolerates will be exceeded by roughly that margin, so leave headroom.

nodes.label: First-reading penalty reported separately
nodes.rationale: Every instrument pays a large one-off on the first reading after output_on() - between 1.3x and 14x the steady figure across this bench - and averaging it into the per-reading number corrupted a figure that is published in choosing-an-smu.md, sets the sweep deadline, and is one of two points _aperture_cost() fits a slope through. The sweep deadline now adds it once rather than per point.

nodes.label: Undalogic miniSMU MS01
nodes.rationale: 12 V, 180 mA, hardware sweeps, small and portable and quick - but not for single-point small voltages. Pick the miniSMU transport rather than Serial: Serial appears to work because the instrument answers *IDN? over it and auto-detection succeeds, and then every method call fails saying a connected, working transport is not connected. 4-wire costs channel 2, because it is a system-wide setting rather than a per-channel one.

nodes.label: Instrument dropdown lists this bench by name
nodes.norm_label: instrument dropdown lists this bench by name
nodes.rationale: The VISA scan asks for GPIB, USB and serial resources by name instead of `?*`, because `?*` scanned the subnet for TCPIP instruments on every refresh. Names come from a table in core/addresses.py filled from this bench's own commissioning reports; the name is only a label, identity still comes from *IDN? at connect.

nodes.label: Per reading is not a ranking
nodes.norm_label: per reading is not a ranking
nodes.rationale: Each figure was measured at that model's own declared minimum integration time and those minima span three orders of magnitude, so a smaller number buys less averaging rather than more speed at the same quality, and two cells are comparable only if the NPLC beside them matches. On the miniSMU the axis is not the same quantity at all.

nodes.label: The miniSMU's nplc column is not a real integration time
nodes.norm_label: the minismu's nplc column is not a real integration time
nodes.rationale: Higher still means quieter and the ordering is correct, but the absolute number is unfounded and must not be compared against a true-NPLC instrument. True NPLC integrates over whole mains periods, which is what nulls 50 Hz hum; this instrument's oversampling is not mains-synchronised, so an 'equivalent 1 NPLC' here rejects hum less well than 1 NPLC on a Keithley.

nodes.label: A serial instrument is recognised by the device, not the COM number
nodes.norm_label: a serial instrument is recognised by the device, not the com number
nodes.rationale: A COM number changes with the machine and the order things were plugged in, so matching is by USB ids (the miniSMU is 303A:82A6, Espressif's vendor id under Undalogic's product id) then by descriptors. No port is opened to find out, because opening toggles DTR and resets an ESP32-based device.

nodes.label: :OUTPut:ENABle output enable function
nodes.rationale: Ties the output to pin 11 of the rear-panel DIGITAL I/O interlock. Already Disable at reset, so the OUTP:ENAB 0 in reset() is reinforcement rather than a fix — it was mistaken for the cause of an output failure on 2026-08-20 and disproved by probe.

nodes.label: :OUTPut:SMODe output-off mode
nodes.rationale: HIMPedance opens the output relay (manual warns of relay wear with frequent on/off); NORMal parks the V-source at 0 V with compliance at 0.5% of full scale; ZERO leaves compliance alone; GUARd parks the I-source at 0 A for guarded ohms.

nodes.label: GSM-20H10 factory reset defaults table
nodes.rationale: Transcribed from pp. 160-164 and confirmed on the instrument 2026-08-20: *RST leaves SENS:CURR:DC:PROT:LEV? at +1.050000e-04 and SENS:VOLT:DC:PROT:LEV? at +2.100000e+01, matching the first two compliance rows. Notable defaults: 105 µA voltage compliance (full scale of the 100 µA range, not a round number), 2-wire sense, 3 ms source delay with auto-delay enabled, auto-off disabled.

nodes.label: Reading the 'Affected by' column of a reset table
nodes.norm_label: reading the 'affected by' column of a reset table
nodes.rationale: Every driver written from a manual so far has had at least one setting whose reset value had to be overridden, sometimes with no command in the log to trace the behaviour back to. A setting reset does not touch needs the opposite treatment from one it does.

nodes.label: ELEMents list defaults to five fields
nodes.norm_label: elements list defaults to five fields
nodes.rationale: Default is VOLT,CURR,RES,TIME,STAT. The driver asks for two and replies have been observed at five regardless; the parser takes the leading pair so nothing is currently wrong, but the driver should not claim the reply is fixed to two fields.

nodes.label: FUNCtion[ON] defaults to CURR alone
nodes.rationale: Voltage is not measured by default, and with concurrent measurement off the voltage column is filled from the source setting rather than from a measurement. This reset table is where the manual admits the fault recorded as 'Concurrent measurement was never enabled'.

nodes.label: Off state Normal makes 0 V on and off indistinguishable
nodes.norm_label: off state normal makes 0 v on and off indistinguishable
nodes.rationale: With Off state Normal the V-source sits at 0 V whether the output is on or off, so a reading at 0 V returns the same thing in both states. Any test of whether the output energised must use a non-zero level; a probe run at 0 V proves nothing.

nodes.label: Rule 12: Configure before energising
nodes.rationale: Once the output is on the sequence sets levels and reads only. The electrical reason matters more than the rule: a mid-run range change leaves a step in the data where two segments were sourced with different gain and offset errors, and a straight line fitted across that step absorbs it as slope — and slope is resistance. No error, an excellent R-squared, a wrong answer. A fixed range gives every point the same systematic error, which largely cancels out of a slope. The sample is protected by whatever compliance was in force when the output went on: IV's periodic standby used to energise a biased sample with the previous sweep's limit or the instrument's reset default (100 uA / 2 V on a B2901A), which damages nothing and is exactly why it survived — the bias is quietly clamped and the file records the requested bias rather than the achieved one. Wave 6b removed redundant per-polarity re-configuration in Van der Pauw and Hall and fixed the range once, before energising, sized to the largest magnitude the run will source; every driver was checked to round up, because rounding down would clamp the source level.

nodes.label: Test suite audit, August 2026
nodes.rationale: Measured at commit 3c456c9 on Linux, Python 3.14.4, single core under xvfb-run; nothing in the tree was changed as a result. Exists to head off two reasonable-sounding instincts the audit found to be wrong: that more test files than source files implies redundancy, and that a newer Python makes plain pytest fine.

nodes.label: :ABORt is not present on the GSM-20H10
nodes.norm_label: :abort is not present on the gsm-20h10
nodes.rationale: Rejected with -113 Undefined header, confirmed by probe 2026-08-14. :TRIG:CLE is the documented route.

nodes.label: bench_result, because a date cannot say how it went
nodes.norm_label: bench_result, because a date cannot say how it went
nodes.rationale: Everything downstream used to infer a recorded last_bench date meant a clean run; on 2026-08-21 the U2722A was checked, failed four checks, and under the previous schema would have rendered 'Verified: yes'. Failing is a distinct status from stale — stale means nobody has checked recently, failing means somebody has and it did not pass. Anything other than pass is treated as failing, so a misspelled value cannot promote a failing driver to commissioned.

nodes.label: What the mutation rounds showed
nodes.rationale: Four rounds, each a single deliberate change with the whole suite run against it. The Hall sign flip lit four files that look like redundancy and are not — they ask four different questions about one line of arithmetic, at a combined cost of ~6 s. The third round made the project's own most-repeated mistake: removing the cancellation branch from RunContext.checkpoint() left test_vdp_lifecycle green, which looked like a coverage hole but was a non-discriminating mutation, because RunToken.sleep() raises RunCancelled independently and Van der Pauw cancels through the pacing sleep. The discriminating fourth round (cancel_event.set() -> pass) lights twenty-one tests across five files at four named boundaries per experiment, each an instant where a stale worker could re-energise a sample somebody has their hands in.

nodes.label: Where the test runtime actually is
nodes.norm_label: where the test runtime actually is
nodes.rationale: 290 s for --all, wildly non-uniform: test_checkup.py alone is 30%. File count costs nothing, so consolidating files would buy nothing and would cost the property that makes a red run readable — a failure naming its own subject. In all six expensive files the cost is waiting, not computing; the GUI files are not paying for Tk (tk.Tk() is 0.046 s) but for the fixed run.sleep(0.04) pacing per reading in the Van der Pauw experiment. That pacing is the highest-leverage lever on runtime and was deliberately left alone: saving ~80 s is not worth touching a queue-drain guarantee inside the experiment that de-energises samples.

nodes.label: Rule 7: A run is a transaction — use begin_run()
nodes.norm_label: rule 7: a run is a transaction — use begin_run()
nodes.rationale: Four non-obvious rules: run.checkpoint() goes before every step that energises or alters the output; register on_cleanup before the claim because an ExitStack unwinds in reverse and the UI must be told idle after the instrument is handed back; the commit sink must not block because the controller's lock is held while it runs; and there is one Stop and it discards — cancellation is a token, the worker de-energises in its own cleanup on the thread that owns the session, and nothing else may talk to the instrument during a run.

nodes.label: State-transition traces hold the ordering
nodes.rationale: The rule is about order, so a test that only asserts each command was present cannot enforce it; the criterion is that a change in command order creating an unsafe or invalid transient fails the suite. Fake transports record the command sequence and simulated state, and five test files assert against it across nine pinned transitions. Ordering and spelling are two claims, not one: an instrument sent an unrecognised command logs it in a queue nobody reads, ignores it, and leaves the previous setting in force, so 'the output-off went out' is not the same claim as 'it went out in this instrument's dialect'.

nodes.label: Compliances the U2722A cannot give you
nodes.norm_label: compliances the u2722a cannot give you
nodes.rationale: Nothing below 100 nA of current or 200 mV of voltage, and nothing between 10 mA and 12 mA, because the current ranges are decades up to 10 mA and then jump to 120 mA so the ceiling of one and the floor of the next do not meet. Placed where somebody picking an instrument finds them before the bench does. A looser compliance also costs a decade of resolution per range step.

nodes.label: On the U2722A your compliance also picks your resolution
nodes.norm_label: on the u2722a your compliance also picks your resolution
nodes.rationale: On every other SMU the compliance protects the sample and the measurement range sets the resolution, separately. Here a limit is settable only between a tenth of the active range and its full scale, so the compliance you type is the range, and the range is what a 14-bit converter divides into 16384 counts: 9 uA gives 0.61 nA steps, 90 mA gives 7.3 uA steps. Setting a generous compliance 'to be safe' costs a decade of resolution per step.

nodes.label: The front-panel current ceiling sets your noise floor
nodes.norm_label: the front-panel current ceiling sets your noise floor
nodes.rationale: Nothing in software can see it. The current accuracy carries a full-scale term of 0.045%, so the floor is 1.35 mA on the 3 A ceiling and 13.5 mA on the 30 A one - on a 10 A cell that is 0.14% or 1.4% of Isc depending on a setting made with a keypad.

nodes.label: On the U2722A the compliance chooses the range
nodes.norm_label: on the u2722a the compliance chooses the range
nodes.rationale: A compliance is settable only between a tenth of the active range's full scale and full scale, which makes the limit very nearly determine the range, so the driver stopped treating them as two knobs. Every limit written is read back because the bench watched a 100 uA compliance silently become 12 mA on a range move.

nodes.label: Multicomp Pro 72-13200 electronic load
nodes.rationale: 120 V, 30 A, 4-wire only by wiring, cannot source. For illuminated solar cells above 3 A where every SMU here clamps, and nothing else. A run refuses anything below 0 V, deliberately: reverse bias needs a source, so sweep the reverse-bias part on an SMU and the high-current part here and expect two files.

nodes.label: Isc and Voc come out of the fit, not the load
nodes.norm_label: isc and voc come out of the fit, not the load
nodes.rationale: The load measures the middle of the curve well and both ends badly. Isc is at V = 0, below the headroom floor, so it must be extrapolated from the low-voltage end; Voc is measured with the input off where the 150 kOhm input impedance leaves the cell essentially open-circuit, so it is not a point on the swept curve. The maximum power point is what this instrument is good at, since the 0.431 V floor sits below the knee. :MEAS:POW? agreed with V x I to every digit at four currents, so treat it as computed rather than an independent third reading.

nodes.label: The CURRent:LIMit example exceeds the instrument's maximum
nodes.norm_label: the current:limit example exceeds the instrument's maximum
nodes.rationale: The page's own example sets 0.8 A while the U2722A's maximum output current is 120 mA — probably inherited from a shared template. Worth knowing before treating any other number on these pages as authoritative for this model.

nodes.label: What the U2722A limit pages do not say
nodes.norm_label: what the u2722a limit pages do not say
nodes.rationale: Recorded because each absence cost bench time and an absence is easy to mistake for something nobody looked for: no minimum (the tenth-of-full-scale floor the driver depends on is undocumented, measured 2026-08-24), no reset default (the 'Default value' column describes the parameter, not the *RST state), no MIN/MAX form so the instrument cannot be asked for its own bounds, no negative or low limit form despite measured asymmetry, and no source-function command at all — which quantity is sourced is decided by whichever of SOUR:VOLT / SOUR:CURR was written last.

nodes.label: What the audit did not measure
nodes.norm_label: what the audit did not measure
nodes.rationale: Said plainly because an audit that reads as complete when it is not is worse than no audit. Nothing was run on Windows; two runtime figures in tests/README.md were not reproduced and were left alone rather than corrected in case they are Windows numbers; and how many absence-assertions are protected only by process isolation was not counted. The audit set out to find redundancy to remove, found none worth defending the removal of, and the honest recommendation was to change nothing.
